newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian workers' income flat in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Canadian workers' income flat in 1995.

text.p: The median income for working Canadians was essentially unchanged in 1995 compared to 1994, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
The median employment income of Canada's labor force was C$20,600 in 1995 or C$24 less than the amount required to keep up with the increase in the consumer price index, the federal agency said.
For men, the median income was C$25,900 and for women it was C$16,000 in 1995, according to data obtained from income tax returns filed in the spring on 1996, StatsCan said.
Both men and women experienced an increase on a current dollar basis, but the gains were not enough to surpass inflation.
The number of Canadians who earned income from employment at any time in 1995 increased by 223,470 from 1994 to reach 14.4 million, the largest change since 1989, StatsCan said.
The study showed that self-employment as a sole or second source of employment grew substantially since the 1990 recession.
But the average amount of income received from self-employment activities was C$13,600 on average, and for women it was C$7,300.
The medians refer to earnings of both full and part-time workers.
